fields.name: can-prepare
fields.label: Can Prepare
fields.sourceQuote: Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can prepare invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: ALIAS COLLAPSE: list-view label 'Can Prepare' (displayed indicator, quote above) == editor-side 'Delegate can prepare' inside the 'Delegate Settings For User Administrators and Employees' section: 'Delegate can prepare: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can create invoices on behalf of another employee.' (create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). The corpus NEVER enumerates a Yes/No or On/Off value pair for this checkbox -- it only says 'If active, ...'. Do not complete that pair. Two-gate model: even when granted here, delegates-submit-a-payment-or-purchase-request-0ee0f0b9.md documents that Can Submit specifically requires a SECOND grant when the user adds the delegate in Profile; the analogous cascading language ('the admin may set the permissions to allow or deny ... from this "cascading" set of permissions the user, in Profile, can select permission levels for their delegate') applies to this control too.

fields.name: can-submit
fields.label: Can Submit
fields.sourceQuote: Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can submit invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: ALIAS COLLAPSE: list-view 'Can Submit' == editor-side 'Delegate can submit': 'Delegate can submit: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can submit invoices on behalf of another employee.' (create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). TWO-GATE MODEL, explicit and named: 'A delegate can submit an invoice or a purchase request for the employee they work on behalf of only if that permission was granted first within the delegate configuration by the User Admin, and then when the delegate was added for the employee. fields.name: restrict-approvers-equal-or-higher-limit
fields.label: Restrict approvers to those with equal or higher authorized approver limit
fields.sourceQuote: If selected (enabled), the user selected to be a delegate for an Authorized Approver must also be an Authorized Approver, with the same or higher approver limit.

CROSS-PAGE: this control's semantics depend on the built Authorized Approval Limits / Workflows Authorized Approvers surfaces -- see dependencyCandidates. contradictions.topic: The name of the Add/Modify Delegate Configuration child surface reached via New or Modify

readings.summary: Called a PAGE, specifically the 'Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice page'.
readings.sourceQuote: Choose New. The Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice page appears.

readings.summary: Called a WINDOW, with the only full menu path given anywhere in this run's file set.
readings.sourceQuote: This window is available by clicking Administration > Invoice > Delegate Configurations > New (or Modify, if existing configuration).

readings.summary: Called the 'Modify Delegate Configuration page' when reached via Modify rather than New.
readings.sourceQuote: Select Modify. The Modify Delegate Configuration page appears.

readings.summary: Called the 'Edit Delegate Configuration page' when linked to from the Name column.
readings.sourceQuote: This is also a link to the Edit Delegate Configuration page

readings.summary: A fifth/sixth reference calls it a 'window' generically AND names the field roster it holds as belonging to 'the Add Delegate Configuration page' in the guide's own revision history.
readings.sourceQuote: select the Delegate can view invoice images for payment requests check box in the Add Delegate Configuration window.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: An automation driving this surface should NOT gate on any single title string to detect the child surface is open. Detect by object shape instead (the Configuration Name field plus the Delegate Settings checkboxes), and accept any of: 'Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice', 'Add Delegate Configuration', 'Modify Delegate Configuration', 'Edit Delegate Configuration' as the on-screen title depending on entry point (New vs. Modify vs. Name-link).
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the surface is a single modal/child-window component whose title is templated per entry point (Add vs. Modify, Invoice vs. Purchase Request) and per authoring pass across this guide's long revision history (dating to at least 2014, see delegate-configuration-8b2bd26d.md), which is why different topics, written and revised independently, settled on different vocabulary ('page' vs. 'window') for the same thing. This graph resolves it as a MODAL ON page.delegate-configurations, not a separate page node -- see identityNotes in the page-level record for the full structural argument (no independent menu destination, no independent role gate, no independent object model).

contradictions.topic: Whether existing delegate assignments survive an employee's move to a new employee group configuration

readings.summary: States the system does NOT remove or update existing delegate assignments on a group move -- it is a manual admin responsibility.
readings.sourceQuote: the system will not remove or update existing delegate assignments.

readings.summary: States out-of-group assignments and now-disallowed rights ARE removed automatically on a group move.
readings.sourceQuote: Any current assignments to other users that are not allowed (that is, are out of group) by the new configuration are removed automatically.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not assume either behavior when automating a group move. Verify empirically (or ask the tenant) whether stale delegate assignments persist or are auto-pruned before scripting any downstream step that depends on delegate state surviving or not surviving a group change.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the two topics may be scoping different things -- assignment EXISTENCE (the delegate relationship itself) versus individual RIGHTS within an existing assignment (e.g. Can Prepare being stripped while the assignment record remains) -- but the corpus never states this distinction explicitly, so it is recorded as an unresolved tension rather than reconciled.

notes:
COLLAPSE CONFIRMED: unique controls on this page number 18 field-shaped nodes above (6 procedural/CRUD buttons -- tab-selector, new, modify, remove, confirm-yes, save -- plus 12 configuration controls: configuration-name, can-prepare, can-submit, can-approve-any-time, can-approve-temporary, can-view-images, restrict-delegates-to-group, need-approver-role-to-approve, restrict-approvers-equal-or-higher-limit, maximum-time-period-to-approve, applies-to-groups, inheritance-toggle). This lands the true configuration-control count at 12, inside the 11-13 band the inventory predicted, well below the original ~25 recon estimate -- the inflation was entirely alias duplication across the list-view/editor/terminology label sets, now collapsed with every label recorded in each field's notes. The two 'Restrictions' and 'Delegate Settings For User Administrators and Employees' section HEADINGS from create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md are deliberately NOT emitted as their own field nodes -- they are organizational groupings over controls already emitted individually (restrict-delegates-to-group + need-approver-role-to-approve; can-prepare + can-submit + can-approve-any-time + can-approve-temporary + can-view-images), and emitting them too would double-count the same controls a third time.

PAGE-HOOD: per the map-phase ruling (repeated here for the record), the Add/Modify Delegate Configuration surface is treated as a MODAL/CHILD WINDOW on page.delegate-configurations, not a separate page node -- it has no independent menu destination (only reachable via New/Modify from the parent), no independent role gate, and no independent object model (it edits the exact same configuration object the parent lists, under different labels). This mirrors the Workflows General/Steps/Step Rules wizard precedent (modal over an object, not a page) rather than the Authorized Approval Limits precedent (its own menu destination and no other home for its fields).

ROLE GATE: none documented anywhere for this page. Confirmed by direct reading of all mustRead files -- no sentence names a required role or permission for reaching Delegate Configurations, creating, editing, or deleting a configuration. The only role-shaped sentences found ('The Configuration administrator can restrict the delegates...', 'The Invoice Admin sets this option when defining delegates.') describe who USES a field or the menu alias, not a reach-the-page gate, and are not recorded as roleGates.

THIN, CONFIRMED THREE WAYS BY DIRECT READING: (1) no Purchase-Request-specific field roster exists in any file read -- the only entry-form title given anywhere is 'Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice'; (2) no start/end date field exists on this page -- 'Choose Dates' points OUT to My Info / User Administration in both of its two corpus-wide occurrences, both inside this page's own rosters; (3) the actual delegate ASSIGNMENT (as opposed to the permission-subset definition) happens on the consumer surfaces (invoice-user-f11cccd8.md: Profile > Invoice Settings > Invoice Delegates / Purchase Request Delegates; user-administrator-5aa3eb5e.md: User Administration), both cited for their identical dependency-worthy sentence ('The columns that appear for the delegate will vary, depending on the settings in the delegates configuration file.') and emit NO field of their own -- confirmed by direct reading, not carried over from the inventory unread.

BOUNDARY DISCIPLINE HELD: emitted nothing from delegate-self-approval-1b627285.md (already built on Workflows as field.workflows.allow-delegated-approvers-to-approve-own-requests) -- cited it only in a dependencyCandidate and in the can-approve-any-time field's cross-references are absent by design; emitted nothing from the audit trail (audit-invoice-delegate-actions-3660a51f.md) which is a behavioral consequence with no control of its own; emitted nothing that would surface the CT_AUTHORIZED_APPROVER database table name from approver-terminology-8559861c.md; did not quote the sample-email block in when-the-delegate-cannot-submit-53c9cb69.md (that file was not read in this pass -- see mustReadSkipped).

UNDETERMINED: whether 'Restrict Delegates to Group' / 'Restrict delegate selection to user's group' interacts with the Authorized Approval Limits group-scoping model beyond the shared 'group' vocabulary -- the corpus never states this explicitly, so no dependency was emitted for it beyond the general Group Configurations cardinality link on 'applies-to-groups'. Also undetermined: exact UI control type (checkbox vs. toggle vs. radio) for the six boolean-shaped configuration fields -- the corpus never shows raw HTML for this page (verified: zero <table> tags in all 18 delegate-named admin files), so 'checkbox' is inferred from the 'If active, ...' phrasing pattern consistently used across all six, not confirmed by a DOM description.
